name: Cat-and-Mouse Thriller
definition: Two aware opponents repeatedly anticipate, test, and counter each other while pressure compresses time, space, and available choices.
negative_signals: danger without an active opposing intelligence
diagnostic_questions: Do both sides adapt to evidence of the other's choices?
Is suspense driven by proximity and anticipation rather than mystery alone?

neighbors.distinction: The adversary is substantially known; uncertainty concerns the next move and outcome.
Cat-and-mouse requires an intentional opponent rather than environment alone.

reader_promises.name: Intelligent counterplay
reader_promises.description: Let each meaningful move reveal information and provoke an adaptive countermove.

reader_promises.name: Tightening net
reader_promises.description: Reduce time, distance, anonymity, resources, or safe choices as the contest develops.

roles.name: Pursued protagonist
roles.description: Acts to survive, expose, protect, or reverse the hunt rather than only flee.

roles.name: Pursuer
roles.description: Uses a distinctive logic, resource, or insight to predict the protagonist.

roles.name: Human leverage
roles.description: Creates obligation, vulnerability, or misleading access between the opponents.

movements.name: Threatening contact
movements.description: Establish awareness between opponents and the consequence of being found.

movements.name: Probe and response
movements.description: One side tests the other and gains incomplete information at a cost.

movements.name: Role reversal
movements.description: Give the pursued party enough knowledge or resolve to shape the contest.

movements.name: Final contest
movements.description: Resolve the central relationship through a prepared choice, trap, or sacrifice.

complications.name: False safety
complications.description: A refuge or ally has already been mapped, influenced, or misunderstood.

complications.name: Shared need
complications.description: Opponents temporarily require the same person, object, or escape route.

complications.name: Collateral choice
complications.description: The safest tactical move would endanger someone the protagonist values.

twists.name: Purpose of the hunt
twists.description: The pursuer wants recruitment, confession, or controlled movement rather than simple death.

twists.name: Watched hunter
twists.description: A third power has been using both opponents to reveal one another.

conclusions.name: Reversed trap
conclusions.description: The protagonist converts the pursuer's method into a credible defeat.

conclusions.name: Costly escape
conclusions.description: The protagonist survives but loses anonymity, relationship, or former identity.

conclusions.name: Mutual recognition
conclusions.description: The contest ends through a choice that acknowledges likeness without requiring reconciliation.

variation_axes.question: What does the pursuer truly want?

subversions: Allow the pursued character to win through social understanding rather than force.
Make restraint, not escalation, the decisive countermove.
cliches_to_avoid: A pursuer who predicts impossible information
quality_checks: Every major countermove responds to observable prior information.
The tightening pressure changes choices rather than only increasing spectacle.
The ending resolves why these two opponents could not disengage.

sources.title: The Structure of Narrative: The Case of Film Scripts
sources.contribution: Provides structural analysis of goal-directed cinematic narrative.

sources.title: Movie Plot Analysis via Turning Point Identification
sources.contribution: Identifies change of plans, setbacks, climax, and aftermath as useful turning-point functions.
